authority: Reference-project design authority delegated by the user: Take the best decisions as the owner and complete the implementation.
scope: Decisions for this reference implementation, not an assertion of upstream API-owner approval or production/sandbox certification.

decisions.title: Account.name
decisions.choice: Optional; accept the published account examples. STRICT_ACCOUNT_NAME is an explicit opt-in interoperability profile.
decisions.rationale: Avoid rejecting valid documented account shapes because of an undefined required property.

decisions.title: Refresh token lifecycle
decisions.choice: Reusable refresh tokens, 30-day configurable lifetime, 10-minute access tokens; code reuse revokes its issued family. No rotation field in refresh responses.
decisions.rationale: Keep the declared response shape and do not assume Uber persists replacement refresh tokens.

decisions.title: HTTP errors
decisions.choice: Unexpected/transient errors return retryable500 on every route, empty when undeclared, and are never cached. Authentication uses declared401, otherwise the existing declared400 mapping.
decisions.rationale: Never misclassify infrastructure failures as final validation errors; minimize unnecessary wire-contract changes.

decisions.title: Cancelled lookup
decisions.choice: Return200 REJECTED for cancelled/expired authorizations by default, with no confirmed_at. ENABLE_CANCELLED_LOOKUP=true opts into the explicit CANCELLED derived-runtime extension. Internal state remains CANCELLED.
decisions.rationale: A successful lookup should describe a known terminal business state rather than return a validation error. This is a visible additive reference-contract extension.

decisions.title: Partial capture
decisions.choice: Allow one positive capture up to the authorization. Successful partial capture closes it and releases all unused hold; preserve authorized_e5 and store amount_e5 as actually captured. Refunds are capped at captured funds; another capture conflicts409.
decisions.rationale: Support a useful payment lifecycle without ambiguous multi-capture accounting or indefinitely retained residual holds.

decisions.title: Capture decline
decisions.choice: Return422 with BANK_HARD_ERROR/BANK_SOFT_ERROR. A definitive rejected capture does not debit and releases the entire original authorization, including a partial-capture attempt. Unknown transport outcomes remain retryable500/reconciliation.
decisions.rationale: Follow the declared error response and distinguish a known business rejection from an uncertain processor effect.

decisions.title: Cancel response
decisions.rationale: Follow the declared response schema; do not invent a response body.

decisions.title: Lookup identity
decisions.choice: Use Uber transaction/refund ID; merchant_reference, if supplied, must match.
decisions.rationale: Follow parameter definitions and keep Uber identity separate from PSP reference.

decisions.title: Rejected callback reference
decisions.choice: Always include an immutable PSP reference, including rejection.
decisions.rationale: Satisfy the required schema and make reconciliation unambiguous.

decisions.title: Authorization-code result
decisions.choice: Code exchange returns refresh token; obtain access token using the refresh grant.
decisions.rationale: Follow grant-specific schemas rather than conflicting sequence diagrams.

decisions.title: Deposit callback routing
decisions.choice: Explicit funding-profile callback routing: new integrations use chargeCallback. Only legacy, opt-in deposit profiles use the upstream-deprecated confirmDeposit/cancelDeposit/updateDeposit. A reduced amount update precedes confirmation.
decisions.rationale: No heuristic routing by transaction ID or funding-code string. Preserve clear flow boundaries and never increase a user-approved hold without new authorization.

decisions.title: Balance request
decisions.choice: Use account_id and funding_method, with scoped account-bound bearer plus signature.
decisions.rationale: Follow the actual operation schema and preserve ownership checks.

decisions.title: Refund wire contract
decisions.choice: Use synchronous201 CONFIRMED then one REJECTED updateRefund by default. ENABLE_ASYNC_REFUND_REVERSAL=false refuses the synthetic two-callback funding profile; true is an explicit reference/test interpretation of the reversal exception. Never suppress an actual financial inverse. Retain declared refund fields/statuses and idempotent local inverse/debt with protected unrelated holds.
decisions.rationale: Follow schemas; implement a durable, auditable local reversal policy rather than contradictory SUCCEEDED/FAILED examples.

decisions.title: Payout identity conflict
decisions.choice: Changed payload under the same payout ID or key returns409 DUPLICATE_REQUEST_ERROR; identical payload replays.
decisions.rationale: Use the declared conflict response and never repeat a payout effect to resolve a key conflict.

decisions.title: Reference settlement
decisions.choice: Closed UTC periods, daily by default; immutable confirmation/reversal journal; one canonical JSONL file per source account with monetary entries (an empty period has an empty manifest) and a checksummed manifest; decimal-string signed E5 and per-currency totals. Seal once, reject overlaps, replay bytes. Atomic directory or strict-host-key local SFTP publication occurs outside SQL; transport receipt is not financial acceptance.
decisions.rationale: Provide a complete runnable reconciliation workflow without claiming the chosen format is an Uber bilateral format or fabricating real hosts, keys, schedules, commercial netting or acceptance.

review_decisions.choice: Return200 REJECTED for cancelled/expired authorizations by default, with no confirmed_at. ENABLE_CANCELLED_LOOKUP=true opts into the explicit CANCELLED derived-runtime extension. Internal state remains CANCELLED.
review_decisions.rationale: Prefer an upstream enum by default without losing the more precise local state. No external enum approval is claimed.

review_decisions.choice: Use synchronous201 CONFIRMED then one REJECTED updateRefund by default. ENABLE_ASYNC_REFUND_REVERSAL=false refuses the synthetic two-callback funding profile; true is an explicit reference/test interpretation of the reversal exception. Never suppress an actual financial inverse.
review_decisions.rationale: Avoid requiring a disputed callback-count interpretation for the default example; do not fabricate external approval.

review_decisions.choice: Description type and maxLength256 remain mandatory. Pattern enforcement is opt-in STRICT_DESCRIPTION_PATTERN=true; default accepts punctuation and Unicode.
review_decisions.rationale: The published example violates its own pattern; never drop escaping or required payment identity/authorization.

completion_decisions.title: Refund reversal callback policy
completion_decisions.choice: Use synchronous201 CONFIRMED then one REJECTED updateRefund by default. ENABLE_ASYNC_REFUND_REVERSAL=false refuses the synthetic two-callback funding profile; true is an explicit reference/test interpretation of the reversal exception. Never suppress an actual financial inverse.
completion_decisions.rationale: Avoid requiring a disputed callback-count interpretation for the default example; do not fabricate external approval.

completion_decisions.title: Payout lookup scope
completion_decisions.choice: Keep find-transaction limited to charges/refunds and return404 for payout IDs. Payout recovery uses original provider-key reconciliation and callbacks; do not add an undeclared public operation.
completion_decisions.rationale: The published scope is sufficiently explicit to make a reference-project decision without waiting for a speculative requirement.

completion_decisions.title: Retention and exact replay
completion_decisions.choice: Purge expired token records; archive operations and DONE jobs older than7days in bounded200-row batches once per minute. Keep unfinished work live and preserve immutable replay bytes, fingerprints, headers and event identities indefinitely in local archives.
completion_decisions.rationale: Bound the hot working set without breaking money idempotency, revocation of live grants, event ordering or financial evidence. This is not a legal real-data retention policy.

completion_decisions.title: Public endpoint abuse controls
completion_decisions.choice: Admit consent via atomic PostgreSQL fixed-minute counters: default200/client and60/peer IP, counting actual peer rather than forwarded headers. Reject with429/Retry-After60 before creating a consent row. Expire old buckets; signed money operations have separate admission. Validated OAuth internal failures redirect server_error with original state.
completion_decisions.rationale: Bound unauthenticated row growth and keep financial locks independent, while retaining external edge controls as deployment requirements.

completion_decisions.title: Runtime and identity stability
completion_decisions.choice: Bind every fresh client namespace to native runtime, storage version2 and independent instrument-key hash. Reject legacy/unversioned populated state, cross-language reuse or silent fingerprint-key changes. Rotating OAuth client credentials does not rotate instrument identity.
completion_decisions.rationale: A fresh namespace is safer than inventing a migration for incompatible replay/ciphertext formats in a no-live-data reference repo.

completion_decisions.title: Semantic release gate
completion_decisions.choice: Run the same independent wire scenarios for every language, including exactly-once ledger witnesses after crash/lost-response,100000-row index-plan regression, bounded public abuse, async/deposit/expiry/duplicate settlement events, multi-source/currency reporting, concurrent seals and commit-clock boundary checks.
completion_decisions.rationale: Operation/status coverage alone was insufficient; require meaningful behavioral and accounting evidence without claiming production scale certification.

completion_decisions.title: Supply-chain and key separation
completion_decisions.choice: Pin all seven base/service images by verified manifest digest and all six official Actions by commit. Run fixture/keygen as non-root; export a public-only gateway key volume and keep the development private key only in the fixture/client volume.
completion_decisions.rationale: Prevent floating dependency drift and avoid granting the Java container access to a signing private key merely because Unix UIDs match.
